definitions.explanation: Maintaining the same attitude, policy, or approach from beginning to end without wavering. Emphasizes steadfastness and lack of contradiction.

examples.japanese: {一貫|いっかん}した{態度|たいど}を{取|と}る。
{彼女|かのじょ}は{最初|さいしょ}から{一貫|いっかん}して{反対|はんたい}している。
examples.english: She has been consistently opposed from the beginning.

examples.japanese: この{会社|かいしゃ}は{企画|きかく}から{製造|せいぞう}まで{一貫|いっかん}して{自社|じしゃ}で{行|おこな}っている。
examples.english: This company handles everything in-house consistently, from planning to manufacturing.

notes:
{一貫|いっかん} literally means "one thread" and conveys the idea of an unbroken line running through something from start to finish.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {一貫|いっかん}して (consistently, throughout)
- {一貫|いっかん}した{姿勢|しせい} (consistent stance)
- {一貫|いっかん}した{方針|ほうしん} (consistent policy)
- {一貫|いっかん}{生産|せいさん} (integrated production)
- {一貫|いっかん}{教育|きょういく} (integrated education, e.g., combined elementary-middle school)

USAGE NOTES:
- {一貫|いっかん}して is the most common form, functioning as an adverb meaning "consistently" or "throughout"
- Often used in business and organizational contexts to describe processes done entirely in one place
- Not to be confused with {一環|いっかん} (part of, a link in a chain), which has the same reading but different meaning
